- S1: the user wants its work run to its end through usage limits, unanswered prompts, and closed
sessions.

session.

- P5.3: the share of pieces stopped by the limit, a wait for an answer, or the session closing is

- ask (skill)\
Hands a piece over as the user words it, so that it runs with nothing left to ask.
- hand-over (script)\
Sets each piece up apart from the person's work and from the session, and starts it.
- runner (script)\
Carries one piece through the usage limit to its end.
- pieces (script)\
Keeps each piece's record, and reports where each piece stands.

more.good_when: A developer who builds the runner and pieces knows from one reading whether a piece that had a tool call refused along the way, yet finished its work, shows as done or as stopped by a wait for an answer, and the README walkthrough's own pieces, whose named tools leave out calls such as a search or `git status`, come out in the status as the README shows them: done, with 0 of 3 stopped.

A developer writing the test cases finds, from the document alone, the expected result of a piece whose call was refused but which went on to the end of its work, and of a piece recorded as running whose runner never started, so no two developers write those cases with different results.

A developer who changes the order of the hand-over's steps learns from the document why the piece is recorded as running before its runner starts, why the runner records its process, and why a resumed piece is recorded as running again, so a change keeps what the status rests on.
